Thank you for the term request. The new term **hybrid osteochondral skeletal cell** has been added to the Cell Ontology as **CL:9900000** (temporary ID; will be replaced by a permanent CL ID during ODK release).

Summary of the addition:
- **Label**: hybrid osteochondral skeletal cell
- **Definition**: A skeletal cell at the periosteal surface of the murine rib that displays hybrid osteochondral properties, emerging within the large callus that bridges segmental rib defects. It derives from a Sox9-expressing periosteal skeletal stem/progenitor subpopulation that constitutes only a small fraction of uninjured rib periosteum. After injury, these cells populate the callus and co-express cartilage and bone regulators Sox9 and Runx2, as well as matrix genes Col2a1 and Col1a1, while exhibiting dual chondrocyte/osteoblast properties.
- **Parent**: skeletogenic cell (CL:0007001) — the formal CL term that the requested "skeletal cell" corresponds to.
- **Anatomical location**: part_of periosteum (UBERON:0002515)
- **Reference**: PMID:30983567
- **Related synonym**: "hybrid osteochondral cell"
- **Contributor**: https://orcid.org/0009-0000-8480-9277
